# Pranks and Mary Jane

April will, in all likelihood, go down as our best-performing month of 2026 — a fact I note with the appropriate amount of superstition. Call it the month of transition. Somewhere between the first cup of coffee on April 1st and the closing print on the 30th, the book turned. We unwound the short positions we'd been carrying since January and crossed the floor to the bull side. The reasoning wasn't sentimental. Positive gamma had pushed into territory you couldn't politely call moderate, and the prime book was flattening the profits we'd accumulated on the short side faster than conviction alone could justify holding them. So we moved.

The data, in retrospect, walked through a minefield without setting anything off. ADP and nonfarm payrolls at the top of the month — clean. CPI — clean. Nothing that pulled the market off the narrative it had decided to tell itself. Today's PCE print is the one I'd flag as carrying a faint hum of latent risk, though I don't want to overstate it. As is so often the case lately, the trouble traces back to oil. The Fed held rates where everyone expected them to hold rates. Liquidity sits at a reasonable level — no flood, no tourniquet, just the kind of unremarkable plumbing that lets price discovery actually happen.

![](/blog/april-2026-illustration.png)

## May and market efficiency

Which is why I suspect May will be the month of market efficiency. Dealer gamma is sitting close to neutral, and when the cushion thins out, prices start doing the work they're supposed to do. I'd expect a correction in semiconductors and a rotation into other sectors — the kind of breadth event that tends to look obvious in hindsight and feel uncomfortable while it's happening. ATROS is anchored accordingly. We're long Chinese ADRs heading into the meeting between the two kings, and we're waiting, patiently, for the right entry to step back into semis. Patience here is the position.

## A closing note

A closing note, slightly out of register with the rest of this letter. I want to take a moment to express my appreciation for Jerome Powell. The man dragged this market — and by extension, all of us — out of COVID, out of more than one edgy situation, and out of a parade of administrative shit shows that would have broken a less steady chair. He is, in my view, the most underappreciated and underrated Fed chair of my career. Time, as it tends to, will tell.

Onward to May. — ATROS W.M.

title: 理解期权订单流及其交易策略
excerpt: 期权订单流的本质是什么？如何据此交易？简言之，期权订单流是特定时间段内各类期权合约的买卖数量，可用于预测个股及指数的走势。
content:
# 理解期权订单流及其交易策略

期权订单流的本质是什么？如何据此交易？

简言之，期权订单流是特定时间段内各类期权合约的买卖数量，可用于预测个股及指数的走势。

这正是成功交易期权必须理解订单流运作机制的核心原因。

![](/blog/5.jpg)

初看期权订单流图表时，可能只呈现为难以解读的箭头符号组合。

但通过实践，可掌握解读技巧，利用图表信息在经纪账户中实现盈利交易。

本文阐释期权订单流的本质，以及交易者如何借此建立优势。

## 核心概念

股票期权作为衍生品，其价值锚定于标的资产。

标的资产即股票。这使期权订单流与股票订单流具有相似性。理解订单流对成功交易者至关重要，因期权流揭示异常大额交易，可洞悉其他交易者与机构的动向。

掌握期权订单流对价格的影响机制，可调整特定头寸的风险敞口，甚至在高影响事件前提前布局。

## 期权流基础原理

交易者需明确三种订单成交方式： 
即时成交 
未来特定时间/日期成交 
未成交 

第二类成交方式即构成期权流。当零售交易者无法确认订单是否通过时，本质在进行观望式交易。

期权流允许市场参与者在未无限期等待成交的情况下实施方向性策略。因期权交易量远低于股票，常出现订单因需求不足无法即时成交的情况。

## 期权流类型

主要存在两类订单流：
卖方流：做市商收到大量客户订单，被迫调整期权报价 
买方流：机构投资者大额订单引发做市商重新定价 

## 订单流分析价值

无论是否接触过订单流概念，深入理解其对盈利逻辑的揭示都至关重要。

## 数学视角的巧合交易

以SPY期权分析为例，对到期前不足1小时的期权进行测算。

对比该时刻未平仓合约量与分钟级交易量，计算每百万张合约中的巧合频次（1张SPY合约对应百万股）。

结果显示：平均每百万张合约存在超20,000次巧合交易。

巧合交易指：买入临到期期权后迅速卖出，或卖出临到期期权后立即回补。

此类情形意味着可合理预判股票短期波动方向。

为验证数学可能性，仅用百万张交易数据测算：每1亿张合约仅出现1次巧合。

## 数据获取机制：非公开与公开组合

当前通过盈透证券等平台可获取实时期权分析数据，但经纪商数据如同雅虎股价信息——可用但效果有限。

核心价值在于同时获取非公开与公开数据组合。

盈透证券等平台使该组合获取便捷且低成本。在"股票科技"框架下，OA本质是交易行为的映射。

## 价格发现的副产品

运作机制：经纪商在期权公开活动结束后，汇总客户建仓/平仓（及行权价调整）订单。

该机制确保非公开活动不被暴露。

## OPR成交交易实例

所有参与者均受影响。

即使自认精通期权交易，也必须认知今日SPY期权（$SPY）的动向。

无论过程是否令人困惑。

无论是否获得解释。

当基于期权订单成交（OPR）交易时，必须理解事件对未来策略的影响。

该认知在当前尤为重要——下文解析后将不言自明。

## OPR机制解析

期权订单成交（OPR） 指标的资产达到期权交易指定价格时触发的执行机制。

当投资者设定期权限定价后，标的股票触及该价格即触发OPR。

## OPR用户群体

挂单买入股票时，需决策未成交是否卖出。

若不欲持有，为何挂单？

OPR成交的核心价值在于洞悉其来源。

毕竟若无用户群体，"专业"即无意义。

OPR是华尔街投行使用的计算机系统。

投资者通过经纪商下单时，指令经多层系统传输。

信息验证过程中同步发送至多家投行，供其判断是否跟单。

若挂单100股IBM限定价$100，前方可能已有1000股买单排队。

## OprFlow最佳时机：择机而动

每周存在订单流异常活跃时段。

这创造双重机遇： 
借OprFlow数据择机建仓 
观察平仓头寸决定是否跟进 

交易期权时，关注OprFlow数据并规避高活跃时段。

在活跃度较低的时段，往往更易捕获稳定价格的优质机会。周边活动减少也降低价格异动概率。

该策略在低成交量日或临近到期日尤具效力——此时期权流数据同步衰减。

## 结论

多数亏损源于对订单流的误读。掌握要诀可建立交易优势：

解读订单流平均提升10%以上收益。

关键在于识别有效信号。作为职业交易者，深谙此道。

>温馨提示：AI 很聪明，但并非万能。在你将投资组合交给 AI 管理之前，请记住：再强大的系统也不是万无一失。市场充满不确定性，即便是最先进的 AI，也难以准确预测每一次突如其来的波动。

>人工智能应作为辅助决策的工具，而非预测未来的“水晶球”。我们诚邀您阅读我们的研究论文：《构建用于金融指导与经济预测的聊天机器人：基于 GPT 大语言模型与搜索引擎数据的探索》

title: Understanding What Option Order Flows Are and How To Trade Options?
excerpt: What exactly are option order flows? And how do you trade them? In short, option order flows are the number of shares in various options that are bought or sold over a particular period of time, and they can be used to predict the movements of individual stocks and indexes.
content:
# Understanding What Option Order Flows Are and How To Trade Options?

What exactly are option order flows? And how do you trade them?

In short, option order flows are the number of shares in various options that are bought or sold over a particular period of time, and they can be used to predict the movements of individual stocks and indexes.

That’s why it’s important to understand how option order flows work if you want to trade options successfully.

![](/blog/5.jpg)

When you first look at an option order flow chart, it may appear to be nothing more than an indecipherable series of up and down arrows with letters on them.

With some practice, however, you can learn to interpret these charts and use the information they provide to make profitable trades in your brokerage account.

This article will explain what option order flows are and how you can use them to your advantage as an options trader.

## Introduction

Stock options are derivatives, which means they derive their value from an underlying asset.

That underlying asset is a stock. This makes option order flows similar to stock order flows. Understanding order flows has always been important for successful traders, as options flow uncovers large and unusual option trades to monitor what other traders and institutions are doing.

As such, knowing how option order flows influence option prices allows you to adjust your risk profile on certain positions and even get in before high-impact news hits.

## The Basics of Option Flow

It’s important for traders to understand that there are three different ways that an option order can fill:

1. Immediately

2. at some future time/date

3. not at all.

The second type of execution—to be filled at some future time/date—is referred to as an option flow. When a retail options trader is executing an option trade and has no idea if his/her order will go through, he/she is essentially entering a wait-and-see option trade.

Option flows allow market participants to take action on their directional bets without having to wait indefinitely for their trades to fill. Because options trade at such low volumes relative to stocks, sometimes an investor’s options simply don’t get enough demand from other investors in order to complete a trade immediately when it hits the tape.

## Types of Option Flow

There are two main types of option order flows: sell-side and buy-side.

Sell-side flow is when a market maker or broker receives a large number of orders from their clients, which causes them to increase or decrease their quotes on options.

Buy-side flow, on the other hand, is when one or more institutional investors (such as hedge funds) place large orders in a particular stock, causing market makers to change their option prices.

## Why Do We Analyze Option Order Flows?

If you trade options, you’ve probably heard of order flow—or maybe not.

Regardless, if you want to develop a better understanding of why option trading is so profitable (and profitable, in general), it’s important that you know what option order flows are and how they can help guide your strategy.

## How Many Coincidences Until Mathematically Impossible?

Using my analysis for SPY options as an example, I ran a calculation on options with less than one hour before expiration.

I compared open interest at that time against total options volume in that minute—as well as previous minutes—and calculated how many coincidences existed per 1 million options traded (since there are about 1 million shares of SPY in one contract).

I found that, on average, there were just over 20,000 coincidences out of a million contracts.

A coincidence is when an investor buys an expiring option then sells it shortly after; conversely, they could also sell an expiring option then buy it shortly after.

In either case, coincidences represent a situation where you’re able to predict with a reasonable degree of certainty that a stock will move by a set amount in a short time frame.

To determine whether it’s mathematically possible for coincidences to exist, I ran another calculation using just 1 million options traded—and found that there was only 1 coincidence out of 100 million options traded!

## Getting the Data: 80% covert, 20% public.

Up until a few years ago, there were no good sources for options order flow information. Now we have options analytics available from big brokers (e.g., Interactive Brokers) that give you access to real-time trading data.

I know many traders who only use OA as their primary source of trade ideas. To be fair, using broker-supplied data is similar to getting stock price information from Yahoo or Google (e.g., you can do it but your results won’t be that great).

The real utility in option order flow information comes when you get access to both public-private and data.

This combo has become very easy and inexpensive with brokers like Interactive Brokers (IBKR) so check them out if you haven’t already! At Stonk Tech its core, OA is basically just information about what traders are doing.

## It’s a byproduct of price discovery.

Here’s how it works: Brokers aggregate all of their client's option orders as they enter or exit positions (and/or change their desired strike prices).

This isn’t done until all public activity in an option is complete, so that private activity isn’t exposed.

## Trading on OPR Fills - An Example

No One Walks Away from this. No one.

Even if you think you know how to trade options, it’s important that you know what happened today with SPY options (the $SPY).

Even if it was confusing.

Even if no one is going to explain it to you.

It happened and we need to understand what it means moving forward when trading on option order fills (OPR) as opposed to just watching them move as they occur live on a screen as they happen.

And it’s incredibly important to know now, because, well – you will see why in about a second once I’ve explained OPR...

The more you trade-in options, or if you’re a novice trader but want to learn, I will give you some solid advice.

### Let’s get started with option order fills...

An option order fill (OPR) is an execution that occurs when a specific price is reached on a stock or index in relation to an options trade.

The way it works is that when you place an options trade, you can specify a limit price.

Which then triggers an OPR once that limit price is reached by way of your stock being at that level or higher.

## Who Uses OPR Fills?

When you place an order to buy a stock, you must decide whether you will sell that stock if your order isn’t filled.

If you don’t want it, why are you placing an order?

Enter OPR fills – what they are, who uses them, and how they can be used in your favor. The most important detail about OPR fills is understanding where they come from.

After all, there’s no point in being a professional if no one uses your services.

To get an idea of who uses OPR fills, you must first understand that OPR is a computer system used by investment banks around Wall Street.

When an investor places an order on his or her trading platform (typically through their broker), it is sent through several computers before it reaches its destination.

This information must then be validated, but it also goes out to various investment banks so they can determine if they want that same trade.

If you place a limit order for 100 shares of IBM at $100 per share, chances are there’s a potential buyer in line ahead of you with a limit order for 1,000 shares.

## Best Times to Use OprFlow: Save the Best for Last.

In any given week, some days are going to see much higher option order flow than others.

This creates a two-fold opportunity.

You can use OprFlow data to determine when to put in a new trade order.

Or you can see which option positions are getting closed out and decide if you want to jump in on that action by opening up your own trades accordingly.

If you’re looking for a good time to buy or sell options, pay attention to OprFlow data and avoid times when there is higher than average activity.

You’ll likely have much better luck at these calmer times of lower activity.

It will be easier for you to find solid opportunities at a relatively stable price. In addition, there is less chance of seeing a big change in an option’s price because there is less activity surrounding it.

This strategy works especially well on low-volume days or when options are moving towards their expiration date since OprFlow data tends to diminish during these times as well.

## Conclusion

A lot of traders lose money when trading options because they don’t understand option order flows. However, there are several tips that you can use to give yourself an edge when trading these products.

By learning how to read option order flows, you can increase your profits by 10% or more on average.

You just need to know what clues to look for. As a professional day trader, I’ve learned how to read option order flows.

# What Are Dark Pool Prints And How Does This Info Help With Trading?

A dark pool print is an important piece of information when it comes to certain types of securities trading.

These securities are only available in the over-the-counter market, which means that these trades aren’t on exchanges like the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) or Nasdaq.

There are also different kinds of securities trading that can happen in this market, and you can learn about them by reading our beginner’s guide to dark pool trading.

When you trade these kinds of securities, you might hear people talking about dark pool prints and wondering what they mean.

Dark pool prints have been around for over 30 years. They allow traders to track their performance and make more money trading stocks than they would without it.

However, the average investor doesn’t even know what dark pool trading is.

Not to mention, how to start using this powerful tool in their own day-to-day trading activities.

If you want to learn more about dark pool prints and how they can help with your stock trading, keep reading!

## Dark Pools

We tell you to question everything. So let's define dark pools.

It's where stocks and other assets trade when no one is looking.

NOT on exchanges but among themselves through computerized matching systems operated by banks, hedge funds, or other 
financial institutions. This can cause a delay in pricing information that could cost you, especially if you try to buy or sell a stock at exactly that time.

While some dark pools enable trades from many different sources, others allow buyers and sellers only from certain pre-approved groups of investors. 

You'd have to read T+3 on a mutual fund trade as an example of a small window for pricing information.These small windows can end up costing you money if you try to buy or sell at just that time.

Many folks say there's simply no way to know how much market prices change during these intervals until they're over.

There is no set definition for dark pools, but many experts agree that when investors lack direct information about available prices, it becomes impossible to determine how prices change during periods of darkness.

The ability to monitor price changes is considered by many professionals to be one of the fundamental skills necessary for market analysis.

In other words, if you don't know how far a security's price moves while it's not visible to you, there's no way you can use that information in your decision-making process.

It's simply unknown information.

![](/blog/4.jpg)

## Dark Pools and Volume

For Stonk Tech, dark pools represent a volume of trading that’s often not made available to the public.

In fact, it can be difficult to detect and follow because unlike securities exchanges like NYSE or NASDAQ, dark pools don’t have a central marketplace.

They’re usually private agreements between brokers and dealers that execute trades in off-exchange markets.

To decipher trade volumes, analysts look at a company’s message board. There, they study dark pool print volumes to determine which of those pools represent legitimate trading.

## Dark Pool Prints

Once analysts have identified that data, they can factor it into their strategy.

For example, a message board will have dark pool volumes from a company’s newly issued shares: insiders that are trading on new company news.

If analysts see large-volume prints in one particular pool they’ll analyze its participants to determine if it’s worth getting involved with or moving forward with our position.

Some companies’ message boards will also publish their volume breakdowns, which can be especially helpful for traders.It allows them to compare different liquidity sources for a company so they can decide which pool or exchange is right for a particular stock.

For example, consider that most big bank stocks trade in dark pools. 

So if a financial institution like JPMorgan announced quarterly earnings, that typically means there will be some movement on their securities. If we see trades in their underlying shares hitting an unusual volume level in one particularly dark pool, we’ll buy into those messages by doing our own research before investing.

The message board will usually break down dark pool volumes with the stock exchange.

Some companies that trade on a particular public exchange may also trade in multiple private pools. That’s why we encourage our analysts to compare their message boards with exchanges like NYSE, NASDAQ, TSX, etc.

## Dark Pools and Price Impact

It’s always a good idea to know where your trading partners are.

With over 98% of all volume now conducted in dark pools, knowing if you’re trading against a dark pool or not is vital.

That said, there aren’t any widely accepted rules for how to price impact should be calculated for orders placed inside dark pools and those placed outside of them.

A small change in an order price can cause a large swing in their price impact.

But when that swing occurs on either side of a large order (and trades in two separate markets), it makes sense to assume that much of that movement is not market-induced but caused by your own initial order.

This kind of Intel is worth remembering, which will help you gauge where you might be having an impact on your trading partners’ prices, allowing you to react accordingly.

Not to mention, how you profit from it.

In recent years dark pools have boomed in popularity: They’re one of many ways that large firms execute trades without impacting share prices.

Like with anything worth its salt, there are pros and cons associated with these types of orders as well.

But what exactly do they consist of anyway?

Orders placed in dark pools aren’t broadcast to publicly traded exchanges until after an order has been executed, which means prices won’t be impacted by its presence on a market.

However, not all orders placed within dark pools remain there.

We're here to bring the dark pool trading to light.

## How Can Dark Pools Help Me Trade Better?

Learning dark pools message board style to help you trade efficiently. If you’re a novice trader, dark pools can offer a better way to learn how to trade.

Learning in real-time can be a dangerous thing when it comes to trading. The fastest traders often dominate, leaving little space for those who have yet to master their craft.

On a dark pool message board, though, there is no time limit. That's because nothing can stop what is coming. As you continue to invest in learning how to trade efficiently, you’ll notice that nothing ever disappears.

The key is to keep your eye on the market as it grows around you. Don't be afraid of those who've already learned from mistakes that are made in front of your eyes. Learning how to trade takes time, but trading is a path best traveled one step at a time.

Everyone learns differently.

You are learning. How many coincidences until mathematically impossible?

Try new strategies out to see what works for you, but never stop reading.

Most importantly, though, keep an eye on how other traders interact on dark pool message boards and observe their successes (and failures).

## Question Everything You Know About Dark Pool Trades

There’s not much information out there about them, so you probably have a lot of questions. We’re here to answer your most important ones! 

If you have experience trading dark pool trades, do you agree or disagree with our conclusions? If you don’t have first-hand experience trading dark pool trades, what questions would you like to ask someone who does?

By thinking logically and making this hidden agenda public, Stonk Tech has created an insightful look into a dark pool trade for traders.

We’ve broken down how we uncovered these secrets in easy-to-understand language so you can make your own investment decisions.

This is where you come in! Remember, let’s trade better, together!

# 什么是暗池成交记录？这些信息如何助力交易？

暗池成交记录是特定类型证券交易中的关键信息。

这些证券仅在柜台交易市场（OTC）提供，意味着交易不会在纽约证券交易所（NYSE）或纳斯达克（Nasdaq）等公开交易所进行。

该市场还存在多种证券交易类型，您可通过阅读我们的[暗池交易初学者指南]了解详情。

当您交易此类证券时，可能会听到人们谈论暗池成交记录（Dark Pool Prints），并好奇其含义。

暗池成交记录已有30多年历史。它们让交易者能追踪自身表现，并在股票交易中获得比未使用时更高的收益。

## 暗池（Dark Pools）

我们倡导质疑精神。因此先定义暗池。

这是股票等资产在无人关注时交易的场所。

交易**并非**在交易所进行，而是通过银行、对冲基金或其他金融机构运营的计算机化撮合系统在参与者间完成。这可能导致定价信息延迟，若您恰在此时尝试买卖股票，可能蒙受损失。

部分暗池允许多种来源的交易，而另一些仅限特定预批准投资者群体的买卖双方参与。

例如，共同基金交易的T+3结算周期就是一个定价信息短暂窗口期。若您恰在此窗口期买卖，可能付出额外成本。

许多人认为，在暗池交易时段结束前，根本无法知晓市场价格变动幅度。

暗池尚无统一定义，但专家共识是：当投资者无法直接获取可用价格信息时，将难以判断黑暗期间的价格变化。

监测价格变动能力被众多专业人士视为市场分析的基本功。

换言之，若您不知晓证券在不可见期间的价格波动范围，便无法将此信息纳入决策过程。

这本质上是未知信息。

## 暗池与交易量

对"股票科技"（Stonk Tech）而言，暗池代表着常不向公众公开的交易量。

事实上，由于其不像纽交所或纳斯达克等证券交易所有集中市场，暗池交易量难以检测和追踪。

它们通常是经纪商与交易商之间的私人协议，在场外市场执行交易。

为解析交易量，分析师会研究公司数据看板（message board），通过分析暗池成交记录量来判断哪些属于真实交易。

## 暗池成交记录

分析师识别有效数据后，即可将其纳入交易策略。

例如，公司数据看板会显示新发行股票的暗池交易量：即内部人士根据公司新消息进行的交易。

若分析师发现某暗池出现大额成交记录，将分析其参与者以决定是否值得介入或调整头寸。

部分公司数据看板还会公布交易量细分，这对交易者尤为有用。它使交易者能比较同一股票的不同流动性来源，从而判断哪个暗池或交易所最适合特定股票。

例如，多数大型银行股在暗池交易。

因此当摩根大通等金融机构公布季度财报时，通常意味着其证券将出现波动。若我们发现其标的股票在某个暗池出现异常交易量，会先自行研究再跟进入场。

数据看板通常会将暗池交易量与股票交易所数据对照呈现。

某些在特定公开交易所交易的公司，也可能同时在多个私有暗池交易。因此我们鼓励分析师将数据看板与纽交所、纳斯达克、多伦多证交所等交易所数据交叉比对。

## 暗池与价格影响

洞悉交易对手位置始终有益。

如今98%以上的交易量发生在暗池，判断自己是否在与暗池交易至关重要。

话虽如此，对于暗池内外订单的价格影响计算，目前尚无广泛接受的规则。

订单价格的微小变动可能引发价格影响的剧烈波动。

但当波动发生在大额订单两侧（且在两个独立市场交易）时，有理由推测大部分波动并非市场诱导，而是由您的初始订单引发。

此类情报值得铭记，它可帮助您评估自身对交易对手价格的影响程度，从而及时应对。

更不用说如何从中获利。

近年来暗池大受欢迎：它们是大公司避免冲击股价的多种交易方式之一。

与其他有价值的事物类似，此类订单同样利弊并存。

但它们究竟包含什么？

暗池订单在执行前不会向公开交易所广播，意味着其存在不会影响市场价格。

但并非所有暗池订单都会停留其中。

我们的使命是照亮暗池交易。
